topic.title: Learning: a 30-minute lesson a day
topic.shortdesc: Your career coach writes a lesson every morning on AI, robotics and PLCs, SaaS and requirements, maker topics or the tools market. Read it or listen to it in the car, and watch your scoreboard grow.

body.p: Every day at 05:40 the assistant picks a topic from your topic map (learning/topics.md in the Brain) and writes a lesson of about 30 minutes into learning/lessons/. The morning brief's last line tells you what it is; tap it to open Learning.

ul.li: Listen plays the lesson's recording. The server records each lesson once, soon after it's written, with a natural voice (free, on the server): whole sentences with natural pauses, chapters for each section, and terms said the way the pronunciation list (learning/pronunciation.md) says. Skip 15 seconds back or 30 on, jump between chapters, and change the speed. It keeps playing with the screen off, and headset, car and lock-screen buttons work. Until a lesson is recorded, a live voice reads it.
A recording keeps playing while you use the rest of the app: a small player sits above the tab bar with play, 15 seconds back, 30 on, and × to stop. Tap its title to go back to the lesson.

The text follows the voice: the paragraph being read is highlighted (untick Follow the voice to scroll freely). Tap a paragraph and choose Listen from here to jump the recording to it; Find my place in the text does the opposite. Where you listened to and where you read to are both saved, on the server, so your phone and PC pick up from the same place, and the lesson offers Listen from where you read or Read from where you listened when one is ahead.

Every lesson shows how far through it you are: a percentage (the further of listened and read) and a bar, and Listened or Read with a tick once done. A recording played to the end marks itself listened, so there's nothing to tap in the car.

In Converse, say "what lessons have I got" to hear them with how far through each is, then "play lesson two", "play today's lesson", "continue my lesson" or "play the lesson about carbide". Lessons under the talk button lists them to tap. A lesson pauses while Converse listens or talks and carries on afterwards; "pause the lesson" stops it.
While a lesson plays, notifications still arrive but without sound or vibration (urgent ones excepted), so the phone doesn't buzz through it.

Not interested? Skip on today's lesson, or Skip this lesson on its page, takes it off To do, Converse and the recording queue (Undo skip brings it back; Skipped in the list's filter shows them). Skip beside a suggested topic means it's never written. Either way the topic goes under Skipped in the topic map, and the coach steers clear of it.
Read opens the text, with a Try it exercise and a quiz at the end.
Mark as read or Mark as listened when you finish, with an optional star rating. Not done undoes it.

body.p: Pick another topic lists what you asked for and what's up next. Make this lesson, or type in Teach me about… and choose Ask: the coach writes it now and it appears in a few minutes. You can also ask in Chat ("teach me about harmonic drives"), and anything you show interest in is added to the topic map.

Topics marked from your work come from what you've been dealing with: each morning, before the lesson, the server notes the day before's chats, your replies and the work you asked for or that ran on schedule in learning/activity/, and the coach turns it into topics. Mail and social messages only count there (how many, about what); their text never reaches the coach.

Lesson narrator, in Settings under Voice beside the voice this device speaks with, picks the voice lessons are recorded with (Learning links to it). Preview plays a sample. The server's own voices are free with no limits; OpenAI and ElevenLabs voices cost per minute.

Every sentence is checked by ear: the server's speech recognition listens back, and an acronym it can't make out is tried spelled out. Under the player, Checked by ear lists anything that still sounds off. Fix the word in the pronunciation list, then choose Re-record. The same list is used for everything the app says aloud, Converse replies included, so a fix there applies everywhere; in Converse you can also just say "you're saying Beckhoff wrong, it's…" and the assistant updates it. Speech uses UK English: British voices, a lone Z said "zed", and British respellings in the list. Recordings are kept with your other files, on Google Drive when it's connected (Command Centre/Personal/audio).

Your streak (days in a row with a lesson done), lessons done, learning time and this week, then lessons a week over the last 12 weeks, lessons by track, and badges. It is counted from each lesson's frontmatter in the Brain.
